title: What is Money? From Barter to Bitcoin Explained Simply 💰
description:
What is money, and how did it evolve from barter to cryptocurrency?

In this video, we break down the complete journey of money — from the barter system to gold, paper currency, digital payments, and modern cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin.

If you want to understand how money actually works and how it impacts your financial future, this is the perfect starting point.

🚀 What you’ll learn:
- What is money and its 3 core functions
- Why the barter system failed
- How gold and commodity money started
- What is fiat money and why governments control it
- Rise of digital money (UPI, cards, online payments)
- Introduction to cryptocurrency and blockchain
- Why understanding money is the first step to financial freedom

💡 Why this matters:
If you don’t understand money, you’ll always work for it.
But once you understand it, you can make money work for you.

📌 This is part of our “Mastering Money: From Salary to Wealth” series on Tejav.

👉 Next Video:
Inflation – Why Your Money Loses Value 📉

---

🔥 Subscribe for more:
- Personal Finance
- Investing Basics
- Financial Freedom
- AI + Tech for Developers

#money #finance #investing #cryptocurrency #bitcoin #financialfreedom

asr.full_text: From chickens and salt all the way to invisible computer code, money is without a doubt one of humanity's greatest inventions. But it's also one of the most misunderstood. So what is it really? And how in the world did we go from trading goats to tapping our phones? Well, let's unpack this incredible story. I want you to just imagine this for a second. You walk into a store. You're ready to buy a brand new laptop you pick out the perfect one head to the checkout and you tell the cashier ok I'll give you say 10 kilograms of rice and two chickens for it sounds absolutely ridiculous doesn't it? Well as weird as that sounds to us today that's exactly how the world worked for thousands and thousands of years. Before money people relied on what we call the barter system If you were a farmer you traded your wheat If you were a Potter you traded your pots simple as that But you can probably guess this system created a world of incredibly awkward really inefficient trades It was held back by one single massive problem that made it almost impossible for economies to grow beyond the most basic exchanges. And that problem has a fancy name. The double-coincidence of wants. But here's what it really means. For that laptop trade to work, you don't just have to find someone who WANTS your chickens. That exact same person also has to have the laptop you want to buy. The chances of that happening? They're practically zero! And that puts a hard limit on pretty much all of commerce. So to escape this trap, humanity came up with one of its most powerful tools ever, The simple, absolutely elegant idea of money! It was designed to solve this trade problem once and for all. You see, for anything to be actually called money, It needs to do three really important jobs. First, it has to be a medium of exchange, you know, something everyone agrees to accept when you buy stuff. Second, it needs to be a unit of account—a common ruler we can use to measure the value of everything. Third, it's gotta be a store of value meaning you can save it today, and it's still worth something tomorrow Unlike a chicken So, the very first types of money weren't paper notes or numbers on a screen No. They had to be things that people already agreed were valuable all on their own Things with what you might call real intrinsic value And this lead us to what we call commodity money We're talking about things like gold, silver or even salt Fun fact, the word salary actually comes from the Latin word for salt, because Roman soldiers were sometimes paid in it. These things worked because they were durable. You could carry them around and pretty much everyone agreed they were valuable. But let's be real. Lugging around heavy bags of gold or big sacks of salt to do your shopping isn't exactly convenient, and it's definitely not safe. Humanity needed a better, more practical solution. and so on. I mean, there are so many ways people can use the technology. One of these is to start thinking about real estate. As you've all already noticed, real estate is a global economy. So when you start thinking about real estate, the word, real estate is the most popular and most popular currency across the whole world. Now, it is important to understand that people buy real estate because it is an incredibly expensive currency — whether it's high or low interest. This was the birth of modern currency, or fiat currency. And this is where things get really interesting. Because it required a massive mental shift. Think about it. A gold coin is valuable because it's made of gold. But fiat money — the dollars, rupees, and euros we use everyday? That's just paper. Its value comes entirely from a government's promise, or fiat — and our collective trust that they'll stand by it. Ah, but a system based purely on trust has a hidden catch. What happens if a government just prints more money? Well, the value of every single note out there starts to drop. And that, my friends, is inflation, the slow, silent thief that eats away at the value of your savings over time. From tangible paper, money then took its next giant leap, into the abstract. It became instant – and, for the most part, totally invisible. Welcome to the digital revolution! This is the world we're all living in right now. Every time you use UPI, swipe a credit card, or check your bank account online, you're using digital money. It's still the same government-backed fiat currency but now it's just data moving around the world at the speed of light. But of course, all this incredible convenience brought a whole new set of dangers. All of a sudden, our money was vulnerable to things like hacking, sophisticated online fraud and some really big questions about our financial privacy and it was these very problems— centralized control, security risks, privacy concerns— that really paved the way for the latest and by far the most controversial evolution in the story of money—The Crypto Revolution— an attempt to build a financial system with no middlemen at all. Kicked off by bitcoin back in 2009, cryptocurrency offered a truly radical new idea. It runs on something called a blockchain, which is basically a super secure public digital ledger that's nearly impossible to tamper with. And its core features were designed to challenge the old systems head on. It's decentralized, so no single bank or government is in charge. And many like Bitcoin have a limited supply. A direct answer to the problem of inflation we talked about earlier. But, and please hear this loud and clear for all of its futuristic promise this new world is also an incredibly wild and dangerous place. This is the space were so many people jumping in without really understanding it end up losing their money. And the main reason is simple extreme volatility the value of most cryptocurrencies can skyrocket one day and then completely crash the next right now it acts less like a stable currency and way more like a high-risk speculative bet so the key takeaway here couldn't be clearer getting involved with complex financial tools like crypto without doing your homework and truly understanding the risks is a massive, massive gamble. So, let's just quickly recap this incredible journey. We started with barter, a system of direct trade that evolved into commodity money based on real, intrinsic value. Then came fiat money based on government government trust, which then went digital, becoming instant and invisible. And today, we're exploring the wild new frontier of crypto, a world of decentralized value. Y'know, this whole story just reminds me of that old saying – if you don't understand money, you will always work for it. Every single step in this evolution created huge opportunities but mainly for the people who actually understood what was happening because at the end of the day smart people don't just focus on earning money they make it their business to understand it understanding how this system works is the absolute first step toward taking control of your financial future and speaking of understanding in our next explainer we are going to zero in speaking of understanding, in our next Explainer, we're going to zero in on that hidden catch in our modern financial world. We are going to dive deep into inflation. And I'll show you exactly why the money sitting in your bank account is losing value every single year. You won't want to miss it.
